title: Cloud–Bulk Interaction Field Equations and the Geometric Origin of the Cosmological Parameter Λ
content: Observations from a wide range of cosmological probes indicate the presence of a non-zero cosmological constant $\Lambda$, conventionally interpreted as a vacuum energy density. However, the well-known discrepancy between observationally inferred and theoretically predicted vacuum energy densities, together with recent analyses combining SNe Ia, $H(z)$, BAO, LSS, BBN, and CMB datasets that mildly prefer models with a time-dependent cosmological parameter, motivate a re-examination of the assumption that $\Lambda$ is a constant vacuum energy density. In this work, we derive interaction field equations from a covariant variational action describing the geometric coupling between astrophysical systems, modeled as localized manifolds (clouds), and a dynamical vacuum-energy background (the bulk). The resulting equations reduce locally to standard General Relativity through the dynamical screening of the bulk-induced conformal sector. The equations demonstrate that the effective cosmological parameter emerges from the isotropic equilibrium of cloud--bulk synchronization, with its value proportional to the background curvature and the residual synchronization of the cloud--bulk boundary. Complementary to alternative $\Lambda$CDM explanations of late-time cosmic acceleration (e.g., entropic or entanglement approaches), the framework provides an effective geometric description in which the small observed value of $\Lambda$ reflects the weakly curved geometry of the nearly flat present Universe, while remaining consistent with observational constraints.
